analysis: The PTY backend's Unix child pre-exec calls setsid(), so the direct child starts as session and process-group leader. The test captures PID/PGID/SID and checks equality before proceeding.

Cleanup filters a ps snapshot by the owned numeric PGID. If any matching row has a different SID, it returns Unverified before per-row start-token verification or any signal. The serialized evidence retains only survivor PIDs, not the foreign row's SID/start token or complete ps output.

Ordinary descendants inherit the owned session. A descendant entering a new session has a separate process group and is not a legitimate member of the old owned group. The foreign-session condition therefore indicates an identity-integrity/reuse or snapshot inconsistency, but these artifacts do not distinguish PGID reuse/race from inconsistent ps identity observation.

Termpane close completed and joined the PTY workers. Its close path then kills/reaps its direct Child handle; this is distinct from sweeping/signalling the process group. Reference exit and group containment remain blocked.
boundary: Preserve the existing no-signal safety refusal. Do not infer a numeric cleanup SID, direct-child exit, reference product success, or candidate qualification from the available serialized records.
